clue.text: Drunk, after small doze, is to recover

indicators.note: after tells us the drunk phrase comes behind the small doze in the answer

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a doze is a nap, a short sleep
out of it is slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: A tipsy person has a quick nap in the hope of feeling better.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to pull yourself together, to come back to a normal state.

clue.text: Succeeded, awful malaise curtailed — they're cured!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly wrong, so the letters are rearranged
curtailed means cut short, so the final letter of malaise is lopped off

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from a terrible feeling of sickness and celebrates being cured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' leaves MALAIS, and 'awful' rearranges it to ALAMIS. 'cured' looks like a recovery from illness; it is meat preserved by salting.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamis are sausages preserved by salting and drying, so they are cured meats.

clue.text: Warnings of changes with temperature dropping

indicators.note: in a down entry, dropping means the letter for temperature slips lower down the word

parts.note: changes as a verb means alters

explanation.surface: Weather warnings are issued as the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves the T of ALTERS two places further down, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerts are signals or notices that put people on guard against danger.

clue.text: Carrying too much round Dover and Deal on tour

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: on tour suggests travelling around, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A vehicle laden with luggage travels round two Kent coastal towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover and Deal are towns on the Kent coast of England; 'on tour' mixes their letters with O.
explanation.definitionFit: Overloaded describes a vehicle or person bearing more weight than they should.

clue.text: Second replacing male in 'Cats' cast

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another within the word for cats

parts.note: toms are male cats

explanation.surface: An understudy steps in for a male lead in the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like the musical; it simply means toms.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast something is to throw it, a direct synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Verge on row with father being superior

indicators.note: in a down entry, being superior means sitting above the other pieces

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A father's position puts him close to being the top man.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is a border or edge, as is a verge, the edge of something.

clue.text: Nail colour beginning to age and crack at edges

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of age
at edges picks the outside letters of crack

explanation.surface: Nail varnish starts to look old and chips at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail colour' reads as varnish; 'Nail' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintack is a small nail, originally of tinned iron, used for fixing fabric.

clue.text: Think live album's second one by character from Genesis

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: second points at the letter in second place in the word album

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Eve is the first woman in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: A fan muses on a live album by the band Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is also a rock band, which suits 'live album'; here it is the Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe something is to think it true or hold it as an opinion.

clue.text: Plot in which there's no survivor?

definitions.text: Plot in which there's no survivor?

parts.words: Plot in which there's no survivor?
parts.note: a story where everyone dies, but plot is also a grave site, where nobody lying there survives

explanation.surface: A grim story in which every character dies.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave plot holds the dead, so nobody in it has survived; it is a cemetery spot.

clue.text: Jane half-cut in small club collapsed

indicators.note: in tells us the half name goes inside the word for club

parts.note: a wood is a golf club

indicators.note: half-cut keeps only the back half of the name Jane

explanation.surface: Jane, rather drunk, keels over in a small nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, which drives the surface; here it halves Jane to NE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, and fainting means collapsing in a heap.

clue.text: Agent departs with shattered tourist carrying kid

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled letters hold the word for kid inside them
shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of tourist are rearranged

parts.note: to kid is to tease, as is to rib

explanation.surface: A travel agent leaves with an exhausted holidaymaker and a child in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges TOURIST as IST...UTOR, which holds RIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A distributor is an agent who supplies goods to retailers on behalf of a maker.

clue.text: Some old-style tome reader brought back from afar

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are taken in the opposite direction
some means only a part of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: An antique book is fetched for a reader from a distant library.
explanation.definitionFit: Remotely means at a distance, as when controlling a device from far away.

clue.text: Cuts risks pronouncedly

indicators.note: pronouncedly means as spoken, so we need a word that matches the sound of the synonym

parts.note: stakes are what is risked in a bet

explanation.surface: Cutbacks plainly carry risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaks are thick slices of meat, the cuts a butcher sells.

clue.text: Fugitives and sailor trick the German aboard ship

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: aboard means the pieces sit inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
to con is to trick
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Escapees and a sailor deceive a German on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Absconders are people who flee secretly, so they are fugitives.

clue.text: Further advanced lesson regularly required

parts.note: A stands for Advanced, as in the A-level exam

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of lesson, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A further, more advanced lesson is needed on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, further means in addition, which is a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Perpetrator of crime wave on most of turf

indicators.note: on places the wave word after the cut-down turf word
most of drops the final letter of the word for turf

parts.note: a lawn is turf, grass
a breaker is a large wave crashing on shore

explanation.surface: A criminal surge sweeps over most of a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks the law is the one who commits a crime.

clue.text: Recording very current European involved in acting

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: involved in means the European letter is placed within the word for acting

parts.note: acting means doing

explanation.surface: Filming a very topical European dramatic performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Videoing is making a recording on video, filming something.

clue.text: Exercise secrecy about source of terrible disease

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: about means the silence word wraps round a letter

parts.note: silence means secrecy, as in a code of silence

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of terrible

explanation.surface: Keeping a dreadful disease quiet is advised.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is an epidemic disease, especially a deadly plague.

clue.text: One enlisted betrayed heartless idle king

parts.note: sold, as in sold out, means betrayed

indicators.note: heartless strips idle of its middle letters, keeping its ends

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A recruit betrays a lazy, cruel monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is someone who has enlisted in the army.

clue.text: Meat Mike fed to dog

indicators.note: fed to means one piece is put inside another, as food into a mouth

parts.note: a lab is a labrador dog
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike gives meat to the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is the meat of a young sheep.

clue.text: Jack in crew working under ace

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means the crew and working pieces sit below the ace

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a band is a crew or gang
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A sailor in a crew works for a top performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack in' is British slang for giving something up; 'Jack' looks like a sailor or playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack in a plan is to quit it, the same as giving it up entirely.

clue.text: Monster from Mediterranean country

parts.note: the USA is a country

explanation.surface: A beast emerges from a nation on the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the snake-haired Gorgon of Greek myth, a monster whose gaze turned people to stone.

clue.text: Improved, knocking out first in league

indicators.note: knocking out first removes the initial letter of the word for improved

parts.note: rallied means recovered or improved

explanation.surface: A team got better after being knocked out of the first league.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means joined together, in alliance, so working in league.

clue.text: Combine tart with nice bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A recipe: put a tart together with some nice bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on each other, to combine in effect.

clue.text: Individual you called 'fool'

indicators.note: called means spoken, so we use a letter that matches the sound of you

parts.note: the word you is said exactly like the letter U
nit is short for nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: One person calls another a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single individual thing, one whole.

clue.text: Knowledge lacking in sport is issue

indicators.note: lacking means the sport letters are taken out of the word for knowledge

parts.note: erudition is deep learning, knowledge
RU is rugby union, a sport

explanation.surface: Not knowing much about sport is a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Revolutionary travelled across Gold Coast, originally a country

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the whole build is read backwards
across means the word for travelled spans the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of Coast

explanation.surface: A revolutionary journeyed over the Gold Coast, once the name of Ghana.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold Coast was the colonial name of Ghana, which tempts 'originally a country' as a definition of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American nation on the equator.

clue.text: Model sat with grin, and hair perfectly in order

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A model posed grinning, with every hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means entirely fine or in good condition, as after an illness.
